newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate, baht ease in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate, baht ease in late trade.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate edged down to 13.50-13.75 percent in late trade on Friday from 14.00 percent early on improving liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said the liquidity was slightly higher today because some banks decided to bring in foreign funds through the swap market to help ease their tight money supply.

"The interbank rate is expected to stay above 10 percent next week. The recent outflow of funds and persistent concern about recent rumours will still affect the market," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The money supply was tighter this week following a rumour in the stock market that some finance firms faced financial problems because their clients might have defaulted on margin loans.

The rumour was denied by the central bank and the Stock Exchange of Thailand but it made commercial banks reluctant to lend funds in the money market on concerns about the ability of the financial institutions, especially finance firms, to repay loans.
The baht fell to 25.394-25.399 to the dollar late from 25.386-25.389 early on dollar's rise abroad, dealers said.
"The dollar/baht trade followed the U.S. unit's movement against the yen. People were buying dollars when they began rising," said one currency dealer.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium was at 11.00/12.00 satangs per dollar late compared with 10.75/11.25 early.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.38 to the dollar, unchanged from Thursday.
